verdict.rationale: Superhuman documents a Cmd+K command palette that can 'instantly do any action' and teaches the shortcut for each one, plus keyboard shortcuts for navigation. A community user corroborates that every interaction can be done from the keyboard, and others praise its shortcuts and fast UI. The 'never make me wait' part is undercut by hands-on reports: archive search regularly took ten seconds, a long-time user cites years of search issues, and another reports occasional crashes. That limits coverage to partial. Missing for 10: consistent independent evidence of no-wait performance (especially search), and first-party documentation of the full shortcut set.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can do everything from the keyboard — comprehensive shortcuts and a command palette — in an interface fast enough to never make me wait

citations.quote: Cmd+K brings up Superhuman Command, where you can instantly do any action — and also learn the shortcut for next time.
In Superhuman, one shortcut rules them all: Cmd+K.
You can reply to important messages faster with blazingly fast shortcuts and features like Instant Intro.
To see your full calendar, just hit 2 or tap the calendar icon. (And hit 1 to jump back to your inbox.)
every interaction in Superhuman can be done from the keyboard, like an email version of vim.
search and UI transitions are blazing fast.
